concept_summary: A full-service restaurant with alcohol service and full cooking at 1463 Haight St in the NCD-HAIGHT district, converting from the limited restaurant approved at this address in 2017 with no alcohol permitted.

overall.line: Of the 4 approvals this concept needs: 1 further review (building permit and change of use), 2 insufficient information (zoning and use, alcohol licence), 1 allowed (health permit).

conditions: Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. Monitoring - After Entitlement (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under P lanning Code Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Nearest and most directly comparable: identical change of use (limited restaurant to full-service restaurant) at 1457 Haight Street, just 13 meters away in the same NCD-HAIGHT zoning district and Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict, decided in September 2024. No construction proposed.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This use decision approved the limited-to-full upgrade via Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 719 and Board Ordinance 249-23, establishing that a CUA is the required path for this intensification in the alcohol subdistrict. The Commission approved it 7-0 with standard conditions including community liaison, three-year validity, and sidewalk maintenance—no special operating…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: The subject property itself: this is the 2017 agency referral (Health Department plan check) that approved 1463 Haight Street as a limited restaurant with the explicit restriction that no alcohol is permitted on-site under Planning Code Section 202.2(a).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral documents the baseline: 1463 Haight was permitted as a limited restaurant in December 2017 with a no-alcohol condition. The proposed concept represents a change of use from that approved baseline, requiring Planning review under the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict rules.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC referral at 1390 Haight Street, 131 meters away in the same NCD-HAIGHT zoning and alcohol subdistrict, decided in May 2021. Shows Planning's stance on license types for restaurants in this corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral was denied for an ABC Type 01 (off-sale beer and wine) because it did not fit the restaurant use, but the decision explicitly stated that a Type 23 (small beer manufacturer) would be approvable for the existing restaurant/brewpub. The distinction matters: Planning approved on-sale licenses tied to bona fide eating places but rejected an off-sale-only license as inconsistent w…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) approval at 1419 Haight Street, 71 meters away in NCD-HAIGHT, decided in July 2019. Agency referral for an existing restaurant adding alcohol.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved a Type 41 license in conjunction with an existing restaurant use, noting it was a continuation of a legal nonconforming restaurant. Planning approved the alcohol addition over-the-counter as an ABC referral without requiring a CUA, but the 2017 case predates Board Ordinance 249-23 (enacted in 2023) that now mandates CUAs for new on-sale licenses in the Haight alcohol…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 approval at 1466 Haight Street (Veganburg), 52 meters away in NCD-HAIGHT, decided in June 2015. Another restaurant adding beer and wine.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved a Type 41 license as a continuation of an existing restaurant use per Section 719.44, handled over-the-counter in three days. Like the 2019 case, this predates Ordinance 249-23, showing that before 2023 restaurants could add beer and wine via simple ABC referral; the new ordinance now channels all new on-sale alcohol through the CUA process.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 approval at 1401 Haight Street, 71 meters away in NCD-HAIGHT, decided in August 2016. Existing restaurant adding beer and wine.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved a Type 41 in conjunction with an existing legal nonconforming restaurant use, processed in 20 days. Again, this is a pre-2023 case that bypassed the CUA process, confirming the pattern that the Haight corridor historically permitted alcohol additions to restaurants administratively until Ordinance 249-23 required CUAs.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health Department referral for a restaurant at 1599 Haight Street, 169 meters away in NCD-HAIGHT, decided in September 2020. Notes the use was permitted under a prior CUA (Case No. 2010.0116C, Motion No. 18079).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral shows that full-service restaurants with alcohol on this corridor have historically required Conditional Use Authorization: the 2020 continuation cited the 2010 CUA as the basis for the restaurant use. This reinforces that restaurant uses with alcohol are conditional, not principally permitted, in NCD-HAIGHT even before Ordinance 249-23.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health Department referral for a restaurant at 1419 Haight Street, 71 meters away in NCD-HAIGHT, decided in March 2021. Same address as the 2019 ABC Type 41 approval.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral approved the restaurant use continuation at the same address that previously added a Type 41 license. The quick 22-day approval for the health permit suggests that once a restaurant use (with or without alcohol) is established, continuations and owner changes are handled administratively unless the use intensifies further.

filing_playbook.action: Attend the Planning Commission hearing and present the application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Present the concept as a full-service restaurant converting from limited restaurant, with alcohol incidental to meals. Cite the September 2024 approval at 1457 Haight as directly comparable precedent and agree to standard conditions. If the census tract is flagged for undue concentration, explain that the restaurant will serve a Public Convenience or Necessity by providing a bona fide eating place with table service, not adding to bar density.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: If a change of occupancy is required (depends on occupant load and existing occupancy group), file the building permit with plans stamped by an architect showing compliance with the Building Code occupancy group requirements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The building permit is for a change of use from limited restaurant to full-service restaurant. If the occupant load is 50 or more, the occupancy group is Assembly A-2; if fewer than 50, it is Group B. Attach the CUA approval as zoning sign-off and coordinate with DPH plan check. If a change of occupancy is required, show ADA compliance, egress, and fire separation upgrades.

timeline_cost.notes: This is a time and cost to approval for the health permit and building permit (if required), which are the approvals in the entitlement path that the rules established. A Conditional Use Authorization—if one is required after the missing inputs are confirmed—would add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 to this range (catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization is not in the path because the zoning row status is insufficient information). The 134–345 day range assumes the health permit (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) and a building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000, plus prerequisite business registration 1–5 days, $55–$700, and health plan check 21–60 days, $828–$2,500, and food safety manager certificate 1–14 days, $100–$250). If the CUA is required the total timeline becomes 254–645 days and the cost becomes $7,316–$34,950. ABC licence time (60–240 days depending on type and transfer vs. new) and cost ($1,000–$450,000) are not included because the alcohol row status is insufficient information. No time or cost is given for formula retail, size over 2,500 sq ft, or hours triggers because those inputs are missing. State and federal registrations (EIN, entity, seller's permit, workers' comp, business registration certificate, fictitious business name) add 4–71 days and $185–$970 but can run in parallel. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) add 2–14 days and $600–$5,000. The September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight took 106 days from filing to approval.
timeline_cost.path: Health permit to operate; Building permit with change of use
timeline_cost.verification_note: Records provide health permit (14–45 days, $470–$1,000), business registration (1–5 days, $55–$700), food safety cert (1–14 days, $100–$250), and 1457 Haight CUA (106 days); building permit, health plan check, combined ranges, and other costs/times not in cited records.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: 1463 Haight St sits in the Haight Street NCD-HAIGHT zoning district, where restaurants on the first story are principally permitted, but the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use Authorization for any new on-sale liquor establishment (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57) serving alcohol. The site was approved as a limited restaurant with no alcohol in December 2017; converting to a full-service restaurant with alcohol is a change of use. The block is heavily saturated: 17 food and drink businesses within 500 ft, 6 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft and 16 within 1,000 ft, triggering the undue-concentration flag. Only three dated use decisions for similar concepts have been filed within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years—too few to compute an approval rate—but nearby restaurant applications with alcohol have been approved, including one just 13 meters away in September 2024 for the same limited-to-full-service upgrade.
